title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is an analytic space or orbifold ('multiplicité'), in the intended application a compactified moduli stack M̄_{g,ν}. Θ ⊂ X is a divisor with normal crossings (the boundary). Θ^{(p)} is the codimension-p stratum. D_d is the space of pairs (point x, choice of d local branches of Θ through x), i.e. the normalisation of the closure of the codim-d stratum, with D_0 = X. For d > d', D_{d,d'} is the space of (x, d branches, a sub-choice of d' of them), with the two natural maps D_{d,d'} → D_d and D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}. More generally, flags d_0 > … > d_r give a semi-simplicial system D_{d_0…d_r}, which Grothendieck calls the '∞-category' 𝒟 of the stratification.

The previous page proved a van Kampen-type statement. The fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood at infinity X^{*∞} is the colimit of Π̃_1 ← Π̃_{2,1} → Π̃_2; codimension ≥ 3 can be neglected.

On this page he wants to localise this along a closed union of boundary strata, presumably to treat the neighbourhood of a part Σ of the boundary rather than of all of Θ.

1. Definition. A closed subset Σ ⊂ Θ that is locally a union of irreducible components of the strata closures D^{(p)} is called Θ-admissible.
2. Encoding by the D_d. For d ∈ ℕ*, let D_d^Σ ⊂ D_d be the union of the connected components of D_d that map into Σ. Admissibility says exactly that Σ is the union of the images of the D_d^Σ (248). So Σ is determined by the subsets π_0(D_d)^Σ ⊂ π_0(D_d).
3. Compatibility for d > d'. The image in X of a component of D_{d,d'} equals the image of the D_d-component under it. Hence the inverse image of D_d^Σ in D_{d,d'} equals the union of the components of D_{d,d'} mapping into Σ. Since Σ is closed, this contains the inverse image of D_{d'}^Σ, but need not equal it. Interpretation: if a critical branch of codim d' lies in Σ, then the deeper codim-d branches contained in it also lie in Σ.
4. Marginal example: a node of a curve configuration in a surface, with D_1 = two lines, D_2 = a point, D_{2,1} = two points. Take Σ = the node. Then D_2^Σ is the point and D_1^Σ = ∅. The inverse image of D_2^Σ in D_{2,1} is both points, while the inverse image of D_1^Σ is empty, so the inclusion is strict.
5. The next page (250–253) defines D^Σ_{d,d'} and D^Σ_{d_0…d_r} as inverse images of D^Σ_{d_r}. This gives a sub-semi-simplicial system 𝒟^Σ ⊂ 𝒟. In modern terms, Σ corresponds to an upward-closed (in depth) set of strata, a sieve/cosieve in the stratification or exit-path category of the normal-crossings pair.
6. A top-margin note proposes generalising to closed Σ ⊂ X (excluding Σ = X), allowing divisors not contained in Θ, with D_0 included.
errors: Internal inconsistency with the next page. Page 76 (250) defines D^Σ_{d,d'} as the inverse image of D^Σ_{d'} and adds '(c'est l'image inverse de D^Σ_d !)'. But this page states, correctly, that the inverse image of D^Σ_d contains, and is not necessarily equal to, the inverse image of D^Σ_{d'}. The marginal node example (Σ = the crossing point) shows the inclusion is strict. Only the inclusion, which is what gives the map in diagram (251), holds.
With Σ ⊂ Θ as stated, D_0^Σ = ∅, so every D^Σ_{d,0} would be empty under definition (250). This is presumably why the margin proposes taking Σ ⊂ X closed with Σ ≠ X.

In the sentence 'on voit donc que l'image inverse de D_{d'}^Σ … est aussi égale à la réunion des composantes connexes … qui s'envoient dans Σ, et contient … l'image inverse de D_{d'}^Σ', the first occurrence must logically be D_d^Σ; as written it is circular or wrong.

ideas.what: Θ-admissible closed subsets Σ (closed unions of boundary strata of a normal-crossings divisor), encoded by subsets of π_0(D_d) satisfying a compatibility condition
ideas.modern_name: closed union of strata ↔ (co)sieve / downward-closed subset in the poset or category of strata (exit-path category, stable-graph category for M̄_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard stratification theory (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie for exit paths; Getzler–Kapranov and Chan–Galatius–Payne for the stable-graph category)
ideas.where_published: The idea of the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n} as a 'tower' appears in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Semi-simplicial system D_{d_0…d_r} of normalised strata with branch flags (an '∞-category' 𝒟), and its sub-system 𝒟^Σ
ideas.modern_name: category of strata / dual complex of a normal-crossings divisor; restriction to a sub-poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, simplicial normal-crossings resolutions); Stepanov/Thuillier (dual complex)

ideas.what: Localising the van Kampen description of Π_1 at infinity (previous page) to the neighbourhood of a sub-union Σ of boundary strata
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid at infinity / of punctured tubular neighbourhood of a stratum; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Harer, Ivanov (π_1 at infinity of M_g), Boggi; Deligne (tangential base points)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is bookkeeping: defining closed unions of strata via components of normalised strata and checking a compatibility condition. It is routine stratification combinatorics. It belongs to a larger unpublished programme (van Kampen at infinity for M̄_{g,ν}), but this page adds nothing new beyond a small internal inconsistency.
transcription_corrections: The first 'image inverse de D_{d'}^Σ' in the 'on voit donc que…' sentence should logically read D_d^Σ; the handwriting is ambiguous.
Under (248) the brace note reads 'réunion de comp. irr. de D_d', then 'donc est connu quand on connaît les D_d^Σ'.
The parenthetical likely reads: '(Cela exprime que si une "branche" critique de codim d' est dans Σ, les branches de codim d contenues dedans le sont aussi)'.
The lower-left marginal sketch is a node example: two crossing lines, D_{2,1} → D_2 (a point) and D_{2,1} → D_1 (two lines with marked points).

The top-left margin reads approximately: 'dire plutôt Σ ⊂ X (s.-v. excluant Σ = X), et demander de ne pas exclure les diviseurs qui ne sont pas contenus dans Θ, tels que D^0 ...'; the reading is uncertain.
Last line: 'La donnée d'une partie Θ-admissible Σ de Θ … [est équivalente à la] donnée …', continued on the next page.
